quality.reason: Well-formatted and transparently discloses its failures, but the signal is 11.5 hours stale from a timed-out scan, one source has been dead for 93 days, and the relayed whale-alert tweets are widely available elsewhere, making this largely redundant rather than actionable.

Well-structured digest with concrete fleet health, PnL, and signal data, but malformed ticker tags ([[]], [["ARB"]]), a truncated news item, and no explicit alerts or recommended actions limit its actionability.

Well-structured dashboard with concrete metrics (scores, margins, declining trends) that serves as a useful status/health signal, but it is primarily descriptive—no explicit alerts or recommended actions despite notable score degradation, and the truncated SOL row limits completeness.
Specific wallet-level position changes with directional flips and size deltas, plus contextual market table (price/OI/funding), make this clear actionable trading signal rather than noise.

Well-structured report with specific metrics, trend deltas, and clear per-agent status flags that identify concrete problems (news-agent single source, stale paper-trader, meta-agent zero output), though it lacks explicit remediation steps and the 15th-consecutive-review note with persistently unresolved issues slightly reduces marginal value.

Well-structured scan with clear methodology, on-topic top papers (LLM-agent orchestration for market research), proper arXiv links and metadata, though the truncated preview prevents verifying the depth of summaries below.

Strong, well-structured signal with real significance (14-15pp Fed repricing with volume context), but lists redundant mirror markets (Sept hike vs no-change, Hike-by-Sept vs Sept-25bps) inflating '5 shifts' to ~2-3 distinct signals, and the output is truncated mid-section.

issues: Verification stamp (2026-08-19) is self-reported and cannot be validated from the document content alone
Verification is explicitly partial: memo and remindctl are NOT installed, so their install commands and syntax were not live-tested despite the 'verified' status line
All three tools are niche third-party Homebrew taps (antonriorodr/memo, steipete/tap) with no version pinning; taps like these frequently move, rename, or go unmaintained, creating dead-link/rot risk
No fallback documented if a tap or CLI disappears (e.g., native osascript/AppleScript alternative), so a single broken tap disables that entire app section
Content is truncated mid-sentence in the iMessage section ('Permission: Gr...'), so the imsg permissions guidance and remaining sections cannot be assessed
imsg path is hardcoded to /opt/homebrew/bin/imsg (Apple Silicon layout); Intel Macs or non-default Homebrew prefixes would break that check
Positive signals: uses current macOS terminology (System Settings, Automation/Full Disk Access), no deprecated patterns detected, and includes a maintenance status block

Tool interface does not match any official API: Anthropic's actual tool is `computer` (beta headers computer-use-2024-10-22 / computer-use-2025-01-24) with actions like `screenshot`, `left_click`, `key`, `type`, `scroll` — not `computer_use` with `capture`, `element=N`, `capture_after=True`. This reads as a custom wrapper but is presented as universal.

Claim 'Claude was trained on both' pixel coordinates and element indices is inaccurate: official computer-use training is screenshot + coordinate based; SOM overlay + AX-index clicking is a third-party prompting technique (Set-of-Mark, AXe-style), not something Claude was trained on.
'There is no Anthropic-native schema to learn' is misleading — Anthropic computer use has a defined tool schema and versioned beta headers; a model-agnostic wrapper still has to translate to it.

The 'background, never steals focus, works across Spaces' guarantee is only true of accessibility-API (AXPress/AX action) implementations, not screenshot-and-event computer use generally; presenting it as inherent to the tool name overgeneralizes and will break expectations if the wrapper changes.

No links, version numbers, or tool vendor/repository cited in the reviewed portion — nothing anchors the doc to a specific tool version, so drift is unverifiable; the action table is also truncated mid-action (`right_cic...`), suggesting the full body needs re-review.

Element indices are capture-specific and expire on any UI change; the doc implies stable indices ('the single most important habit') without warning that indices must be re-captured after state changes beyond the immediate `capture_after` result.

References to 'GPT, Gemini' computer use are plausible for 2025 (OpenAI CUA/Operator, Project Mariner) but are uncited; if this skill predates those APIs reaching general availability, model-capability claims may be stale.
Review based on truncated content (first 2000 chars only); the Fleet Data Quality Pitfalls row is cut off mid-sentence and the remainder of the body is unverified
Reference files use relative paths (references/*.md) whose existence cannot be confirmed from the excerpt alone; freshness relies solely on the self-reported 'Last reviewed: Aug 23, 2026' claim
Self-reported verification ('all 5 references verified present; fleet domains current') is not independently corroborated by anything in the visible content
Mentions of specific internal artifacts (planner.py, external_signal_accuracy table, fleet DB checks) can only be validated against the live codebase, not the doc itself

Minor: two update dates present (Jul 4, 2026 and Aug 23, 2026) — no staleness, but the nested 'Updated' note inside the subsystem table is a pattern prone to drift if not maintained alongside the top-level review date

No deprecated tools, dead external links, or obsolete patterns detected in the visible portion: Obsidian, cron, and the agent-loop patterns (generate/critique/rewrite, maker-checker, bounded execution) are all current paradigms

Only the umbrella skill body was provided; the three files under references/ (claude-code.md, codex.md, opencode.md) could not be inspected for stale commands, flags, or dead links, so this assessment covers the index only

Core technical content (SoM capture, AX-tree indexing, AXButton/UIA Button/AT-SPI 'push button' role names, background non-focus-stealing automation) is accurate and current — staleness is confined to the tooling/dependency references
Core git patterns (merge/rebase conflict resolution, worktrees, merge-queue arbiter, AGENTS convention) are current — nothing deprecated in the underlying workflow
